thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu_queue_size for pool 'v15-prod-gpu' exceeded 85% for 6m. Autoscaler failed to add nodes due to quota/scale_limit. Paging team: @jamie-oncall, @luke-sre, @priya-eng
jamie-oncall: seeing this — dashboards look ugly, 5xxs rising from 1.2% -> 9% in last 10m. Where's the spike coming from?
luke-sre: initial grep shows queue_depth rise correlated with model v15 rollout at 2434480000. tail of logs indicate heavy KV cache warmups, lots of large-prefill requests.
priya-eng: yes we pushed v15.1 last night; model's default context window changed to 64k tokens for a subset of endpoints (we thought it would be limited). Can confirm some customers started hitting long-context prompts.
marta-ops: autoscaler logs: `scale_request denied: pool_quota_exceeded` and `instance_launch_failed: vendor_quota` interleaved. Also saw throttles: `throttle_rate=0.7` on routing layer.
jamie-oncall: customer impact? ben-customer-success any reports?
ben-customer-success: two customers reported timeouts via support: ID# 3012, 3015. Both on high-throughput chat endpoints. Not yet P1 escalations but churny.
eva-product: can we narrow to a specific route? could be one of the high-throughput tenants using the new context mode.
luke-sre: routing traces show a traffic spike from tenant: aiwidgets-prod on route /chat/stream; they started a large rollout 30m ago. Their average seq_len jumped x6.
priya-eng: their SDK started sending `context_hint: full_history` flag by default in 15.1 — my mistake. That enabled full memprefill behavior.
jamie-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback v15.1 globally 2) patch server to ignore `context_hint` for hosted tenants 3) force throttle aiwidgets-prod 4) add temporary GPU capacity (if vendor quota allows). Which is fastest?
luke-sre: fastest is throttle aiwidgets-prod at edge and enable short-term fallback model (v14) for canary traffic. We can also open vendor support ticket but ETA > 30m.
marta-ops: can enable burstpool but quota prevents adding more GPUs; we have ReservedPool at 20% but it's already mostly used.
priya-eng: I can push a hotfix to reject context_hint longer than 8k for hosted tenants in 5m. Will that stop kv warmups?
jamie-oncall: yes that'll prevent new warmups but won't drain existing large KV caches or queued requests. Need queue drains and throttles.
jamie-oncall: luke, can you apply rate limit 10rps on aiwidgets-prod and route 20% of their traffic to v14 immediate-fallback?
luke-sre: on it. Applying limiter now... `ratelimit apply aiwidgets-prod 10rps`
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: route-split v15->v14 for aiwidgets-prod (canary 20%) by luke-sre at 2434510200
jamie-oncall: priya, please start hotfix to ignore context_hint > 8k for hosted until we have opt-in flags.
priya-eng: creating patch branch now. I’ll push a config that enforces `max_context=8192` for hosted default. ETA ~6m to deploy.
ben-customer-success: notifying affected customers: telling them we are mitigating with throttles and may see degraded tail latency. Will offer status page updates.
eva-product: add note on product incidents page that v15.1 changed context default; will craft user-facing messaging after root cause confirmed.
luke-sre: queue length is dropping slowly after throttle; GPU utilization still high due to KV cache warmups. Some in-progress requests still eating memory.
marta-ops: we can try aggressive KV eviction on warmup path: set `kv_prefill_ttl=30s` for new sessions — can be toggled via runtime flag. That would reduce memory pressure but might increase latency on some flows. Thoughts?
jamie-oncall: acceptable, flip the flag if we need more breathing room. Do it after rollback decision.
priya-eng: hotfix deployed to staging, canary to prod in 2m. Will disable `context_hint` behavior for hosted.
jamie-oncall: luke, once hotfix is live, start draining queued requests and re-evaluate autoscaler.
luke-sre: hotfix live at 2434511200. Observed new requests respecting 8k cap. Queue growth stopped, new warmups reduced ~85%.
jamie-oncall: start draining: set pool drain rate high and mark new nodes as unschedulable for v15 until capacity stabilizes.
luke-sre: drain started. Also requested vendor quota bump; vendor replied 'processing' ETA unknown.
marta-ops: enabled `kv_prefill_ttl=30s` globally for hosted at 2434511600. Seeing memory free up on GPUs, some recovery in 60-90s.
jamie-oncall: good. Monitor errors and latency. Ben please update customers with 'mitigation in progress, throttling applied, expected recovery 30-60m'.
ben-customer-success: message sent to affected customers, waiting replies.
eva-product: flag for postmortem: release process allowed a default-change to propagate to hosted without opt-in. We need a release gating rule.
priya-eng: taking ownership of postmortem. Will include diff, rollout config, and suggested guardrails.
jamie-oncall: oncall handoff in 45m; I'll include notes. Current status: GPU queue dropping, autoscaler not yet able to scale due to vendor quota but immediate impact mitigated via throttles+hotfix.
luke-sre: metrics: queue_depth down from 950 -> 120, 5xxs falling to 1.8%, latency tail improving. Keep watch.
jamie-oncall: last check — any other tenants showing abnormal seq_len growth?
luke-sre: no, only aiwidgets-prod and a small staging tenant. Both contained.
jamie-oncall: OK switching to monitoring/retrospective mode. Handoff to @priya-eng for postmortem and @luke-sre for infra follow-up. I'll update incident channel and close paging unless things regress. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated, severity -> P2, owner -> priya-eng, followups -> postmortem, infra-sla-review, release-gating. Timestamp: 2434513599
jamie-oncall: handing off. Good job team.
priya-eng: I'll document timeline and the rollback plan for v15.1 feature flags. Assigning follow-ups to release and runtime owners.
luke-sre: will work vendor quota + autoscaler resiliency stories. Leaving watches for next 2 hours.
ben-customer-success: will follow up with customers and close tickets if no further impact.
jamie-oncall: closing thread for paging. Remaining notes in the incident doc. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
